utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We may have some technical difficulties with the computers, it appears, and therefore we may have to have some inconvenience and delay if they arise. Let us hope that that does not present a significant problem. It, of course, delayed our commencement this afternoon. It has been pointed out that while we received oral submissions during this week in respect of the motion concerning a witness contemplated by the Prosecution next week, Ms. Cakar, with a view to protective measures, that the Chamber did not announce its decision at the time that it dealt with another similar motion. We will correct that now so the position is clear when the witness is called next week. In the Chamber's view, it would not be open to it or appropriate in the circumstances for protective measures to be granted in respect of this witness. I won't go into detail in respect of the reasons. In summary, the reasons offered in justification do not, in the view of the Chamber, come within the scope of the Rule that would allow protective measures to be granted; and, of course, in construing that Rule, the Chamber has to maintain a balance between the basic procedure and its guarantee whereby the proceedings of this Tribunal are public against the interests of a particular individual and of justice in allowing in very special circumstances a witness to be able to be heard with protective measures which limits the public nature of the proceedings. So in the circumstances in this case, the Chamber will not grant protective measures as sought. So we now continue with the evidence of the witness. Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: May I just remind the witness before you commence that the affirmation made at the beginning of your evidence still applies. Yes, Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I continue questioning the witness, the Defence has a new binder with documents. We would like to disseminate those so we do not interrupt the session, the examination, so we do not interrupt the examination later on. So I would like to ask the court usher to provide the rest of the documents to the Court Chamber, the Prosecution and the witness. Of course, since the number of the document is quite large, I would -- I will say that maybe we will show only 10 percent of these documents, and the rest of the documents are a basis for questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can we say, Ms. Residovic, that the Chamber, in its years of sitting in cases, has never before had such a volume of documents for one witness. I hope it does not become the pattern for future witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps that will happen in the future, but I think for several of the witnesses you could hear, the Defence was in a situation -- such a situation that we will to look at all available documents and this will, of course be very rare, but it happens. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, General. You remember when you told me yesterday that you know that after the events in Bitola. There were arrests and criminal prosecution of larger number of individuals. As you have said yourself there were about 100 individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to look at the document at tab 97.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I start asking questions about this, this is a list of individuals who -- who have had criminal reports filed against them. Since we -- when we were asking [indiscernible] a previous witness, we submitted his statement for identification 1D125 for identification. I would like to say, bearing in mind your decision from yesterday, I would like to submit this document for identification so that the Defence can obtain the criminal reports that are listed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In this response, you can see that two lists of individuals are listed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I'm told that this document is not under the number that I gave. In order not to keep waiting on this, when we find the right number I'll come back to this question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you said that in the solving of the crisis all measures were undertaken in order to solve the crisis in a peaceful manner, yet, on the other hand, there were military and police measures in order to counter the attacks of the diversionary terrorist groups. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have also mentioned that you have yourself, as a member of the posebna, you were put under the command of the military in the course of a joint military police operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not just in one. On many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, General Risto Galevski also took the witness stand in front of this Court. He also testified about the manner of commanding in these cases, and you have yourself talked about it on the first day of your appearance in front of the Court. Since in the course of the re-examination of the witness, in the opinion of the Defence, there was a need to put forward additional questions to the General. I would like to look at the document at -- beyond the table 86.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to say right away, Your Honours, we do not propose to put this document as evidence, but I would like to ask a few questions. This is document 65 ter, which is in page -- which is at tab 86A and has the number 65 ter 1D604, page, the Macedonian version is 1D5457, and the English one is 1D5460.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 18th of July, Risto Galevski, was asked by the Defence of Ljube Boskoski the following question. And this is what he has answered. I'm quoting the parts of the transcript. "Question: So when your police forces, regardless whether those were the Tigers or the posebna unit, when they participated in the fightings against Tetovo, Vaksince and other areas, then basically they were acting upon the single command of the army. Is that correct?" This is the transcript for July 18th on page 3750. To that question, I answer the following: "Practically I couldn't say it was so, but together with the military command we used to sit together and work jointly. Also, the question remained open who is superior to whom and who commands to whom." This was said on page 3750 of the transcript during the re-examination of the Prosecution, on several questions asked upon the Prosecution are answered in the following manner. "Question: Yesterday on page 3750 from the transcript, you also explained that -- that during combat operations carried out by the police and the army in 2001, the question remained open who is superior to whom and who commands whom. Do you remember explaining that to the Chamber? "Answer: I think I said it and I will repeat it now. There was a dilemma within the state leadership while those of us from the Defence leadership we did not have any problem and we did not care about who is in charge of what. We were just interested how to do our job professionally. "Question: Okay. So but in a practical sense, during those joint operations the police commanders retained some level of common authority over the police in their units. "Answer: I don't understand you. Who were the ones that had command authority? "Question: I'm sorry. So during those joint operations in which both army units and police units were involved, police commanders, commanders of the police units, retained some level of command authority over the police officers in their units. "Answer: Yes, of course. "Question: For example, the police commanders that participated in those joint operations could have still disciplined their subordinates for infractions or misconduct. Would that -- would it be appropriate to say that? "Answer: Yes, of course they could." This is the transcript from July 19th, 2007, pages 3831 to 3832. Asked by the Defence to clarify what I thought, what -- by giving the aforementioned answers those shown?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Might I interrupt you at that point. Are you now moving to something that has occurred out of Court since this witness gave evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to put an opinion to the witness and to see whether he agrees with it or not. And I would just propose that this is marked for identification and possibly as 92 bis statement would be then sent to the Court at the time when the Defence leads its evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm wanting to be clear: Are you now moving to some discussion that you have had with a witness who was here after that witness completed his evidence about the content of his evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. We sent him a telegramme asking him to explain to us his position regarding the pages that I just indicated here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you want to put his answer to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to ask this witness who had stated previously that he was subordinated to the army structures to see whether that reply is correct, whether this is how it was done in the practice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has been discussing what is contemplated and let me put to you our position very simply and clearly. You may certainly ask of this witness his position about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You cannot put to this witness what has been said out of court since evidence was given by a witness. You may put to this Court what the witness has said in court, but not what has been said since then out of court. If there is some basis upon which you believe that the Chamber should now hear that witness again about some aspect of his evidence, you will need to move or leave to re-call that witness. And that is whether it was a witness for the Prosecution or your own. The witness, having given evidence, having been cross-examined on it, having completed his evidence, the only way that that evidence is be supplemented or varied is if you persuade the Chamber that the witness should be re-called. And certainly you may not, in a second-hand way, put to other witnesses what that witness has since said about his evidence. Is that clear enough?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Completely clear. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, considering that you were subordinated to the army units, could you tell me whether it is correct that at that moment you received the orders from the army superiors who were effectively your superiors during that time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a commander of the eastern posebna unit in the crisis region where we operated, Kumanovo and Tetovo, before any operation we would sit down with the military commanders. We would agree on the procedures on the way in which we would act, how the army will act, how the police would act. Actually, orders were issued to both the police and the army. I, as the responsible superior officer for the posebna unit, communicated those joint, those agreed orders at the level of platoon commanders and the unit commanders, and they then issued commands to their soldiers. I wish to clarify that at the joint meetings orders were issued that were executed by the operational commanders who had the direct command over the police officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that joint agreement where you were present, considering the unit you have command, was the final order issued by a military commander or someone else?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last word belonged to the military commander, who kept a military log with the deployment of the army and the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now my question is: Is it correct that you, the police officers, continued being in -- within the Ministry of Interior although, within that specific operation, you were ultimately subordinated to the orders of the army commander?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if a member of the police, during that operation, would do something unauthorised or illegal, regardless of whether it is a criminal or disciplinary offence, would it be correct that then the military commander, who is in charge of that operation, would have the duty to produce an information about that and to inform the subordinate -- the superior police officer?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was taken care of at the morning meetings. And we also had evening meetings, where it was presented what has done -- and what needs to be done in the time to come. If any of the police officers would violate any rule or if they abused their powers, that was presented at those meetings and then appropriate measures were taken against those in proportion to the offence that has been committed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So for a police member who participates in the operation where they are subordinated to the army commander it is the army commander who would need to inform the superior police officer about that, regardless of whether it would be a unit commander, under-secretary of the police or any other subordinate police officer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, superior police officer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, then this superior officer would make measures as described by the police rules. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But if the army commander would fail to inform the police superior officer, then of course the police superior officer would not know or would not be able to undertake any activities. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You also stated that the president of the state is the supreme commander, commander in chief of the Armed Forces pursuant to the constitution and the law and that he did perform his duties during the crisis. If I remember well, you stated yesterday that in that capacity of his the president of the republic could have ordered the use of police forces and placed them under the command of the army. Was I able to understand your answer of yesterday well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that the president of the Republic as commander in chief, was able to order performance of a joint operation and to decide the way in which these operations, this action would be commanded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could the president, according to his legal powers, issue that order, order on taking the command over that action to the police forces as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: We spoke earlier that the president declared invalid the decision of the minister about the demobilisation of the reserve forces, so if I state that you are aware that not only president could have, but that he actually did issue orders by which he issued activation of the police forces would this correspond to the practice that you were aware of, the practice of 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the president, as the Commander-in-Chief, was able to issue orders in writing, orally, or via messenger?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I were to say that it was within his legal and constitutional powers that he, as the Commander-in-Chief is able to undertake the command of some action personally if that is his decision, then you could agree with me, that this was also possible?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a customary practice that the president would be in command, but the president has the right to decide whether he personally would take command or issue an order to somebody else to command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. After the signing of the Ohrid Framework Agreement, you, together, with the representatives of the international community, started working on the return of the population, especially return of the police to the former crisis areas. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That plan for return meant taking full control over the territory comprised by the crisis and also enabling the police to perform all its legally prescribed duties. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So only after the police was able to return to these areas that would be the guarantee for the safe return and life of the citizens that were displaced during the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That plan involved three stages, or three levels of return, depending on the degree of security risk in that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You personally, General, worked with the representatives of the international community, especially the OSCE on the plan for the return of the security forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now that a video is shown. The transcript of that video is in tab 163, and that is Exhibit P276. The sound is not activated.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: "THE INTERPRETER: [Voiceover] Police General Risto Galevski went into some detail to spell out the plan to employ the security forces to re-establish complete control of the territory of the Republic of Macedonia. The plan is intended to enable the safe return and comprehensive security of all citizens, freedom of movement and realisation of all human rights and freedoms. The plan was jointly prepared by the General Staff of the Macedonian Army, the Ministry of the Interior, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the international community. In the first stage of this plan the security forces will reenter the villages with the lowest level of risk. In the Skopje area these are Gorno and Dolno Mojance, Orlance and Ljuboten; in the Kumanovo region, Vaksince and Lojane; in the Tetovo area Lesok, Tearce, Slatino, Varvara, Brezno, Dobroste, Odri, Jelosnik, Prsovce, Otusiste and Glogji. And in the Gostivar area: the settlements of Gorna and Dolna Banjica as well as Pozarane village. Galevski explained that there had not been any military operations in the settlements but they were under security risks due to the presence of the terrorists. The second stage would involve the Macedonian security forces entering medium risk settlements; and the third phase would re-enter settlements with the high level of risk. Special plans --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, in this video, you recognised the Minister Boskoski, the director of public security Goran Mitevski and the under-secretary for police Risto Galevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see the video. I was only listening.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the video was not displayed on your screen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask for just a sequence of this movie to be repeated so that I'm able to ask questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is not a problem, I could go look at it on another monitor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please just show the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is fine now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able now to recognise in this video Minister Boskoski, the director Goran Mitevski, and the under-secretary Risto Galevski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that this plan was presented as early as in September 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And as we heard from the elaboration that the under-secretary presented here, Risto Galevski, at that time it was considered that the security forces will enter Ljuboten in the first stage, considering that Ljuboten is one of the places with the lowest level of risk, of security risk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was Ljuboten entered in the first stage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was not entered.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the security situation at Ljuboten village was very difficult and that there was a resistance of the population to the police entering the village, and there were new incidents developing so it was necessary to change the plan. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 164. This is Exhibit 1D138. The page is 1D4333 in the English language and 1D4332 in Macedonian. General, this is the annex to the general plan of the 23rd of November, 2001. Does that annex already envisage a change --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: -- about the return to certain places?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now Ljuboten is considered among the places that are at high degree of security significance.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you develop maps in the preparation of this plan, and did the maps have markings in colour that depicted the risk level or the high risk under which certain settlements were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I participated in that.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like now that we show the map. That is 65 ter 1D605.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Since this map is quite large, it is a bit difficult to open it in e-court, but we have this map also at the chart here, the flip chart. So until the map -- the map opens on the screen, maybe the witness might be able to explain on this map what were the colours used to mark the places with certain degree of security danger. We can now see it in the -- on the screen as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell us what colour was used to mark the most dangerous places where it was most difficult to return the police there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Green.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you -- at the map that you see in front of you, are you able to circle the places that are marked in green?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you enlarge the map a little bit? In the middle part of it. Could you please enlarge it a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, regardless that I don't see this map enlarged, would you -- could you find the place of Ljuboten on this map?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please enlarge? We can't see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So please mark -- you're marking them with red dots, but please mark the green ones.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Ljuboten is marked in green. That is the third stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If that is the village of Ljuboten, do you recognise the greens? I asked you to mark the green colours. Could you see the green colours?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I mark the green-coloured fields or ...

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The green ones, the most dangerous places.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Is the village of Ljuboten among these places as well? Are you able to find it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where is the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's here.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you put the number 1 next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you said that you yourself participated in the preparation of this map. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And at the time of preparation of this map, Ljuboten was the place with the highest degrees of risk for the return of the security forces. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this map in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D178, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look into the document in tab 166. That is Exhibit 1D140. And it is in tab 166. Exhibit 1D140, page 1D4246. That is not that exhibit. 1D140.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, this is the main plan for the return from December 2001. And is that the final plan that marked Ljuboten as a place of the highest degree of risk for the return of the security forces?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if it is -- if it would be possible to tender in evidence also a map that has not been marked, as well as the one that was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the original map will be Exhibit 1D179.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, the reasons that Ljuboten was treated in this way is because in and around Ljuboten, groups of the so-called ANA continued to be seen there and the forces that continued to attack the army and the police forces. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to ask now, with the assistance of the usher, that a document is given to the counsel and to the witness. This is a document that originates from NATO, and we received this document from the Prosecutor. Before the start of the session, we tried to put it in e-court, and if it is uploaded, it is 1D1 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D608.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the document, that was submitted to you - we only have this one available in English - which comes from the Allied Press Information Centre Skopje, light forces for southern Europe, the following is said. "[In English] Terrorist attack army position near Ljuboten summary. Yesterday late in the afternoon about ten Albanian terrorists attacked the position of Macedonian army near the Skopje village of Ljuboten. There are no injured soldiers. The army responded to the attack. It is supposed that the terrorist group and the Macedonian from Kosovo." [Interpretation] General, are you aware about these facts about the attack that happened in the beginning of December 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now look at the document in tab 165. That is Exhibit 1D139. The page is N004-9830. And the English version is N004-9830-ET. And as you can see, this is an information of the Ministry of Interior from the 7th of December, 2001 about the security situation in the crisis regions. And please now, if you turn to page 3, the Macedonian number is N004-9832, while the English one is N004-9832-ET, and 9831-ET, in fact. In the second paragraph in the Macedonian language and in the last one in the English version, it is said -- the following is being said: "In the Skopje region on 3rd of December 2001, in the area of the village of Ljuboten at the locality Basinec and Kolash Mara, a group of several armed persons attacked the positions of the army of the Republic of Macedonia which attack was returned. The exchange of fire lasted until the group withdrew into the first houses of the village of Ljuboten from where they once again acted towards the Armed Forces. There are no injured soldiers in the attack." You recognise that this information of the Ministry of Interior speaks about the same event that was mentioned in the information of NATO. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this NATO information, tender it as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not see how this document produced by NATO, the media analysis section, advances any of the issues that are relevant to this proceeding. This news report says that there was an attack by a so-called group of terrorists against a Macedonian army position near the village of Ljuboten. Nothing more than that. We don't know how near or how far. It then says that it is supposed that the terrorist group entered Macedonia from Kosovo. So nor do we have any information that these so-called terrorists came from the village of Ljuboten. Indeed, the information in this report is exactly the opposite. So the Prosecution doesn't see how this report is relevant to this proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you also refer to the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, I -- it is certainly outside the time-period of the indictment, Your Honour. I feel that some level of leeway can be given to the -- to the Defence position that if there is information that members of the NLA were present in Ljuboten even after the 12th of August that could be relevant to these proceedings. But this is long after that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I understand well, the Prosecutor's case against our client, Mr. Boskoski, is that he did not take measures to investigate and punish at least until May 2002. And as far as I can see, December 2001 is within the time-frame of the indictment that speaks about the responsibilities of Mr. Boskoski to investigate and punish. In respect to the second question, that is very relevant because the witness said that the police forces were not able to even enter and not even carry out police tasks in the village of Ljuboten because of the severe security situation. This document exactly confirms a part of that response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Being in a generous mood on Friday, Ms. Residovic, the Chamber will receive this document as having potentially some faint relevance to the issue of armed conflict.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D180, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, that this process of the return of the security forces in the crisis areas lasted for quite a long time and that it would not -- it wasn't possible for it to go without the assistance and the help of the NATO representatives and the representatives of the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Later also the American Embassy got involved through the ICITP programme. Also other international organisations were involved there who helped in their own way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you agree with me if I were to say that in the first stage that entrance with the presence of the NATO forces and the OSCE was just a daily patrolling without the possibility to take any other police activities in the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it true that the first patrol with the assistance of the Amber Fox, that is to say the NATO forces and the representatives of the OSCE entered the village on the 2nd and 3rd of January in 2002, entered the village of Ljuboten in order to just carry out a daily patrol through the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that regardless of the fact that the police entered the village during that day, it was until very later that the police was able to carry out its police duties in the village of Ljuboten and also in the other villages in order to service summons to hear persons detain persons, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look into the document in tab 172. That is 65 ter 1D588, and the page is 1D5371, and the English page is 1D5372. It is 65 ter 1D588. It is in tab 172. General, this is an OSCE document, and it is sent to the General Mitevski, Goran Mitevski, and to General Zoran Jovanovski. Are you the person who was the under-secretary of the uniformed police on the 4th of June, 2002?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This NATO document -- I apologise, OSCE document discusses the plan for the return to the normal performance of the police duties in order to be able to -- in order for the police to be able to exercise all its functions. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does it mean, General, that until the 4th of June, 2002, the police was still not able to perform its police duties normally in the areas at risk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this now goes beyond the period of the indictment, but I still seek to tender this document in evidence, considering that it indicates whether the police was able to perform its duties also beyond May 2002.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As 1D181, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to these issues that you discussed now, the issue of freedom of movement and the issue of check-points can be mentioned. Considering that you stated that you cooperated with the OSCE closely, is it correct that the OSCE started objecting to the insufficiently quick removal of check-points from some of the crisis regions. This happened in the fall.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, General, that actually the check-points given the overall defence structure during the crisis were established in order to prevent access of sabotage terrorist groups to the settlements and to the places comprised by the crisis?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. An assessment is made, a security assessment of a given region, and then the locations where check-points will be installed are determined. These check-points perform control of the movements of citizens or they are placed at the locations where movements of such terrorist groups, as you call them, are expected. So this is in accordance with our plans.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So is that correct that this basic security assessment of a given region is performed by the police of that region, the units for internal affairs, and for the regions comprised by sectors, then the assessment would be made by sectors for internal affairs?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Every head of a sector together with the other superior officers develops the plan and identifies the locations for the check-points to be installed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 87. That is 65 ter 1D562. 1D5149 is the page in Macedonian language, while 1D5152 is the page in English. I said that they were in tab 87. General, you see that this is a document issued by the department of internal affairs, Cair, and it is actually an overview of the locations where there is a possibility for the Albanian terrorists to emerge, and an overview of the locations of vital importance that could be targeted in the attacks at the area of the Cair municipality and the document was issued on 26th of April, 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you look now at the page 1D5151, and the English page is 1D5156. And is it correct, General, that considering this assessment performed by the department for internal affairs, Cair, an overview of the check-points was made, check-points in the area of that municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 88. That is 65 ter 1D563, the page is 1D5157, and the English page is 1D5160. This document was generated before the previously mentioned document, and as you can see, it was an addition to the plan for physical and operational coverage as of April 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This annex or these additions to the plan were produced by the police station Mirkovci. That is within the Cair department. And it covers the area going in depth towards the border.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we look at the second page, which is 1D5158, and the English version is at 1D5162, we see there that actually this annex of the plan, as you mentioned, was produced by the Mirkovci police station, the commander, and it was approved by the head for the sector for internal affairs, Ljube Krstevski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does this example show that actually the check-points in the field were identified on the basis of the assessment of the local police stations and local police departments who were best able to know what is the level of risk in their region?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if we can agree on this, the minister did not participate and the minister did not influence the identification of the check-points at a given area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even if the minister wanted to the participate, the minister could not cover all the regions; so, in no way had the minister participated in the generation of these plans.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender these two documents in evidence as Defence exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 1D00562 will be Exhibit 1D182. 65 ter 1D00563 becomes Exhibit 1D183.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Some time ago you mentioned that during the implementation of the Ohrid Framework Agreement that the international community started to make comments at one time why the check-points are not removed from the crisis area. Is it true that these comments or -- that these comments of the international community were primarily coming about the part populated with Albanians?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that the entire plan for the return envisioned gradual abolishment of the check-points, also having in mind both the Albanian and the Macedonian population?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like that we look into the document found in tab 131. It is 65 ter 1D577. 1D5316 is the Macedonian page, while 1D5378 is the English page. This is a report from a meeting that the Minister Boskoski and Director Mitevski had on 5th of September 2001 with the assistant of the general secretary of NATO. Daniel Speckerd. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting as it can be seen from paragraph 2, the minister presented certain problems connected to the freedom of movement and was informed that NATO is reviewing these issues in detail. If we look the last paragraph of this page, the one before the last in Macedonian, we can see that Minister Boskoski answers to certain comments that, allegedly, the Lions and the posebna are at the check-points. And in respect to that Minister Boskoski says the following: "The Minister Boskoski, expressed the following with respect to what has been said, that there are members of the reserve composition of the police at the check-points but not members of the ESZ and the PEP. That is the special tasks unit --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is the special tasks unit. The special tasks unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tigers or posebna?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Posebna.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Regarding the attitude of the police, the Minister Boskoski stated that: "All members of the MOI have been given Rules for acting of the security forces and that anyone who breaches the authorisations will be held responsible pursuant to the Law on the Interior." At the next page the minister says: "Precisely because of the big number of this information which are acknowledged about the behaviour of the police, Minister Boskoski agreed that there be NATO representatives who will be present at the check-points at all times and who will have a clear picture of the situation at the check-points which is a good way of persuading the international community and the NATO that all the accusations in that respect are pure disinformation." General, are you familiar with the fact that the minister proposed and that NATO and the OSCE have accepted to gather with the police to be present at the check-points in the crisis areas in order to avoid the unsubstantiated accusations that were coming anonymously against a certain number of police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. NATO has its own work methodology, and they were not present with us at the check-points but they had their patrols that were patrolling the area and they had certain periods where the -- where they visited the check-points and where and when they exchanged information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Although the witness corrected me, I would like to say that I -- this ESZ abbreviation that I used in Macedonian, that I misinterpreted that this is the Lions and not the Tigers. So this is the special tasks unit. Does that report show and confirm what you said yesterday that in order to warn for a certain overstepping of authority by the police you gave large authority both to the international community and, at the same time, you distributed to all check-points and police stations rules about how the rights of all persons should be observed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We wanted to work publicly and transparently.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this exhibit as Defence exhibit as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D184, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now look at the document found in tab 132. That is 65 ter 1D578. 1D5320 is the page, while the English page is 1D5321. General, this document was published on the 10th of December, 2001 in Macedonian and in English, and in Albanian. And is this also one of the further measures that you undertook in order to accomplish what you, as you responded to my question to do, to make the police as much professional as possible and to protect the citizens?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is one of the things that we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the documents found in tab 133. That is 65 ter 1D579, which is page 1D5322 in Macedonian, and 1D5326 in English. This is the cover page about the police and human rights handbook on -- handbook for the police. And if we look at the second page, 1D5323, and 1D5327 in English, one can see that this publication was published in 2003. And now, please, look at page 1D5325, and English is 1D5328.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 29. 1D5329.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if you were able to find the document, that is a forward to this publication, and it says: "The successful publishing of the first 2.000 copies of this handbook led to increase in the interest for the use of the information entailed in it. Bearing this in mind, the Helsinski Committee of Macedonia began a cooperation with the department for the development of the police from the organisation for security and cooperation in Europe and the Ministry of Interior for providing training of the Macedonian police within the mandate for police training of the OSCE, all with the aim of meeting the needs of the MOI with respect to the human rights and the police training and the proposals of the committee for prevention from torture." General, is it obvious from this forward of this publication published in January 2003, is it clearly visible from it that the -- that the ministry has distributed 2.000 copies to -- copies about the basic rights and duties that the police must protect in exercising their duties?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And let's just look at the document found in tab 134. That is 65 ter 1D544. The page is 1D4991, and the English page is 1D4992. General, you spoke yesterday that -- you distributed to the police officers and to the police stations notice about the rights of the citizens. Is this one of the ways in which you tried to warn for any kind of overstepping of authority of the police in cases when you were not able to -- to prevent every specific case or to detect any overstepping of authority made by certain police officers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This information about the rights also refers to these parties and the police officers, the parties to be informed about their rights and the police officers who work with the parties to be warned that the parties have the rights that are mentioned there within.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence would seek to tender these exhibits in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect to the document that is at tab 133, police and human rights handbook on police training issued by the Helsinki Committee on Human Rights in Macedonia, the Prosecution notes that this document was published in January 2003, clearly long after the period of our indictment, and it was published two months after the accused, Mr. Boskoski, left his post as minister of the interior. So the Prosecution doesn't see how this document will advance any of the questions that are material to this case. With respect to the document that is at tab 134, there is no information put -- available to us as to when this particular notice was created or distributed. And without that information, I don't see how this particular document can be relevant either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in connection to this document in tab 133, we would like to indicate -- we only indicate to the forward which speaks that this document have -- came after the successful distribution of the previously published 2.000 copies. If something has been published in January, in the previous 2.000 documents were published before that, supported by the testimony of this witness that is the time when Ljube Boskoski was in charge. If we also look into the -- his conversation from 4th of September, that the Minister Boskoski had with the representatives of the international community, even at that time he informed the international community that all the police officers were given a manual about human rights. Out of these reasons, we think that this forward, because of its content indicating about the measures taken by Mr. Boskoski should admitted. Regarding the last document at tab 134, the Defence was not able to determine the date of publication of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document at 133 will be received in evidence on the basis that it is, in a sense, a second printing of a document printed within a time more relevant to these proceedings and the role of the accused Mr. Boskoski. The second document at tab 134 will not be received. It has no time reference that would enable any determination of its relevance to the issues in this case. So the first document, the Helsinki Committee Report will be received in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we tendered also the document in tab 132 that is dated 10th of December, 2002, and the Prosecutor did not complain to it, so we would also seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter number 1D00578 becomes Exhibit 1D185. And 65 ter 1D00579 becomes 1D186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time? We will adjourn until 20 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, tell me, please, is the vicinity of Jezince village also one of the locations that were under strong security risk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look at the document there tab 98. That is 65 ter 446, N005-1552, and the English is the same number, just with the ET appended. This is, General, an information from the Ministry of the Interior -- no, that is not the number. 65 ter 446. The number is N005-1552. Yes. This is an information to the information agency sent by the Ministry of the Interior, and in the second paragraph it reads: "Yesterday around the midnight in the vicinity of the village of Jezince, near the place called Ciganski, Grobista, extremist terrorist groups armed with automatic weapons attacked three security check-points at the Vratnica reserve police station and at the entrance to the village of Jezince. After that, part of the terrorist groups retreated to the other side of border, towards Kosovo, Socialist Republic of Yugoslavia." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to correct you. It is not the reserve. It is the reserve police station.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the third paragraph from the bottom -- in the second paragraph from the bottom it is stated: "In this information, once again the MOI urges the population of both Macedonian and Albanian nationalities to stay away of any provocation and to remain calm because the Ministry of the Interior is undertaking all necessary measures to maintain peace and in that way, we urge them to contribute to the implementation of the President Trajkovski's peace plan." My question first, General, is whether this information confirms that the Ministry of Interior tried to resolve any problem in a peaceful manner?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the second question I have to ask you with regards to this is: As you stated previously, but let's confirm it once again, that the village of Jezince and this area was even later, so in the fall of 2001, an area where the security situation was under significant risk?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the village of Jezince is located immediately next to the border with Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And for the Macedonian security forces, especially for the police, it was of particular importance to control that area so that it could prevent entry of parts of terrorists groups from Kosovo into the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was only the security reasons which were the basis for maintaining the security check-points in that region, even later. So as far as the third stage of -- of the removal of check-points?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I may clarify. The regional road leading from Skopje to Tetovo, after Jezince, there is a part where Macedonian population lives that is Vratnica and because there is Macedonian population there, and the regional road is there, the check-points were -- the check-points were left until later there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The witness who testified before this Court and his consolidated statement, as 92 bis statement is Exhibit 231.1. In his statement to the Prosecutor on the 18th of February, 2006, and in London, in March 2006 as well, on the 9th and 10th of March, stressed-- and that is Exhibit 236.1, received under the 92 ter rule not 92 bis. And in this statement which he gave to the investigator of the ICTY, Thomas Kuehnel, he asserted that such things as removal or instalment of check-points were under the competence of the minister. I will read to you item 7 which reads: "I used to work at the medium level in the Ministry of the Interior. I thought that the standard operational decisions in a modern police department would need to be issued by the minister who is focussed in the modern police systems on the strategic decisions. The tension in the chain of command was exhibited through the extreme rigidity and inflexibility by a part of the medium and higher level of police administrators of medium level within the high police leadership. Everyone was afraid of making decisions and everything was left to the minister. For instance, there was a police check-point at the village of Vratnica, near Tetovo, the presence -- the presence of this check-point was quite dubious because the ethnic Albanian population objected to its existence and its existence was in breach of the local cease-fire agreement according to which both parties needed to withdraw from the road Tetovo-Jezince. The OSCE advocated the removal of this check-point, but the police, at the actual position where the check-point was located, informed us that the minister decided that the check-point must remain where it was, and it really was even strengthened." General, tell me, was the minister personally ever deciding on which check-point would be removed and which one will remain or did this decision depend on, as you testified earlier, the security situation in the respective region which was assessed by the local bodies as well and it was also a component of the defence of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assessment of the security situation was the basis for the establishment or abolishment of check-points. The minister could never issue such decision whether to abolish or to establish any given check-point.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So in a situation or when the situation on the field so requires, the police, in order to protect the entire population, the police, police in general, and particularly the minister, could not decide whether a check-point would continue existing or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I have already stated that it was Exhibit P236.1. And considering that I did not quote the paragraph from the consolidated statement but rather from the statement that the investigator took from the witness, I assumed the obligation to give you later the exact paragraph in the consolidated statement of this witness. General, since we saw several documents where it is clear that the international community was involved, were you, in the police, absolutely clear that could you not perform many of the tasks in the field without cooperation or assistance of the international community?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it also correct that at the beginning, the international community rendered full support to the efforts of the Macedonian authorities?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at one point in time you felt that there was a shift in the position of the international community, and that the level of support that used to exist is not there anymore?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you personally have been the representative of the ministry to communicate with the international community on numerous occasions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And I would like to ask you now to look at the document in tab 151. That is Exhibit 1D133. That is N005-1626 is the Macedonian page, and N005-1626-ET is the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And until we wait for the page to be loaded, we found in the mean time the respective item in the consolidated list; so I wish to state for the transcript that the paragraph that I read was item 27, paragraph 27 of the consolidated statement. Apologise, 27 of the witness statement and considering that the witness testified publicly, it was the witness Henry Bolton.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have in front of you, General, the information about the meeting with the representatives for the KFOR, meeting at 19th of July, 2001. You were the representative of the ministry, you personally at that meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in that meeting as well, you expressed full preparedness to cooperate with the NATO forces and you asked that the process of disarmament starts, proposing that other international organisations participate in it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting with KFOR was important for you because it was completely clear that the logistic support to the NLA groups comes from Kosovo and that only with KFOR's assistance you will be able to repress such terrorist attacks. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, we will now go on to a completely different topic, and that refers -- the questions of the committee that my learned colleague asked you about. You -- in the beginning you were speaking about the competences of the ministry. You said that the ministry is authorised to establish also ad hoc committees. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the commission established by Hari Kostov in March 2003 which you presided with, was also an ad hoc commission, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these committees were not able to carry out procedures that are the competence of the outer bodies of the ministry of the interior, of other standing bodies, especially not procedures that, according to the law are in the hands of the Prosecutor's office, the courts, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a professional in the police, as a president of that committee, you -- it was clear to you that the police has no authority according to the Macedonian laws to interview persons as witnesses. It is under the -- in its competences -- that is under the competence of the criminal police and collect information from the citizens. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information that the police would gather in that way from the citizens could serve to the police to gather other evidence that these informations would indicate to, and could create conviction among the police that there is a minimum amount of doubt in order to file a criminal report. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The information that the police was gathering in their regular line of work, that information was also the information for the Prosecutor in order to decide whether some facts mentioned in the criminal report are sufficient to request initiation of a criminal procedure or to request additional activities by the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But -- however, this information were not -- could not be sent to the court and could not be a basis for a court decision. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 21, we should correct what I asked. I asked, this information or statements were supposed to be put aside from the court files and could not serve as a basis for a making decisions by the court. The witness responded to that question. My learned colleague the Prosecutor showed you a decision for the establishment of the commission that you recognised and that is Exhibit P379 MFI. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And you -- you confirmed that these are the tasks of the committee that were established, that these tasks were broadly determined, and that in your discussions with the minister you agreed that the commission would carry out that part of the work that was -- that it was possible to do. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision did not prescribe the way of work of the commission and in the commission, you agreed among yourselves how you are going to carry out your work?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There's no rule how the commission would operate for any commission. The commission itself is the body that will agree about the manner in which they -- it will work.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the way of work or the procedure that you adhered to was not a procedure set forth by the Law on Criminal Procedure, or by the collective agreement about how a disciplinary procedure that was initiated. That was a procedure that you agreed among yourself about how to carry out your work?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I understood you well, you said that you called the persons over the telephone or in writing?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Then you would interview those persons, but as far as I was able to understand, that interview was not conducted pursuant to the Law on Criminal Procedure as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you clarify what "yes" means, was it conducted or was it not conducted?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not conducted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: According to the documentation that was shown to you by my colleague the Prosecutor, we can only see -- we can see only one summons to Johan Tarculovski for the second meeting of the commission whereby in that summons it has been indicated to him that he can hire a lawyer and he was warned that if he does not appear that he is going to be brought in. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: No other person was called in such a manner, but mainly they were called by telephone and with the regular written invitation, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The others were called only over the telephone.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the information produced out of the work of your commission where an interview would be carried out, it would -- it wasn't written if a person was warned about the rights that person has when interviewed. Is my understanding that you did not warn those persons about any rights correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The persons were not warned. Also, their rights were not told to them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you never told those persons that -- that they are not obliged to speak at all. You never warned them that their statement might be used in court. You never warned them that they are not obliged to answer any of the questions that would incriminate them or their close relatives, that would put them -- made them a subject of a criminal prosecution or cause any material or moral damage to them nor you warned them about other rights that must be mentioned in a criminal procedure?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not carrying out neither a criminal nor a misdemeanour procedure. We only carried out some unofficial conversations, internal conversations with those persons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you explained, every commission as well as this one had a representatives for the sector for analysis that kept minutes and on the basis of those minutes an information was prepared. And that information was also prepared by a person from the analytics department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When I asked you yesterday in which way the information was sent from the operational headquarters Ramno, you said that the headquarters Ramno would review the information and that that information would be then sent by the analytics sector to the minister. Was the same manner used in this commission as well?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So once you would review the composed information and you would find no comments about them, then the member of the commission, that is to say a member of the analytical department, would send the information to the minister and would register it in the records of the sector for analysis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So Mrs. Groseva, if I can say so, would be in a position to better say what has been sent to the minister than you would be able to say or that other members of the committee would be able to say. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if Mrs. Groseva testifying before this Court would say that it was a normal practice and that happened also with your commission, that she sent the minister only the information without the attachments, the Official Notes, that some of the interviewed persons made, then that would be different than what you said, and what do you say? Is it correct what Mrs. Groseva said?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The minister only receives the final information, the final version of the information or the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when you answered to the questions of my learned colleague that the minister received also the Official Note, was that your assumption or did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So from the meeting an Official Note might -- might be prepared, a report, or minutes. That is a final document that has three names so to say: Official Note, report or minutes it all depends on the person that would make it, and the person who -- who would make it would title it in certain way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And don't you think that Mrs. Groseva testifying before this Court would make a mistake about what she used to send to the minister bearing in mind that the sending of the document was her duty in the commission. Do you think that she didn't make a mistake?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: She didn't make a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also said that the commission was gathering information for the minister, but in the tasks that you were given by the minister, it was mentioned that you have to determine the responsibility of the persons. Tell me, please, is it possible at all for your commission or for any commission that was not set forth by a law or a general act to determine some individuals' responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's only one commission within the Ministry of Interior who makes such inquiries. That is the disciplinary commission. The other commissions have no authority about it at all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, have the right to issue decisions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understood you well, you were especially not able to determine anyone's criminal responsibility. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The composition of the commission that was shown to you was such that practically covered all the relevant parts of the Ministry of Interior that act pursuant to the law and that by its line of organisation from the lowest to the highest parts of the ministry were able to provide the relevant documents and minutes to the ministry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And bearing in mind that composition of the commission, do you think that the minister could rely that your commission would carry out its tasks to the extent possible?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said you knew that in 2001 another commission was established by Minister Boskoski. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that commission, as well as yours, was an ad hoc commission, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Its composition as obvious from that decision, contained the most responsible officials of the Ministry of Interior and that is the bureau for public security. That is to say, the director was there; the director of the bureau, Goran Mitevski; the under-secretary for the police, Risto Galevski; as well as the under-secretary for the criminal police, Zivko Petrovski. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: These persons were managing the most important parts of the police. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And they had the opportunity, through the lines of their management, from the sectors and department in the municipalities to gather all the information that these public security bodies possessed. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You already said that you have a very high opinion of these persons. My current question is: Bearing in mind their position that they had in the ministry and their professional and personal characteristics, are those persons to which information the minister was able to rely?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, completely.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the -- the tasks of your commission mention that you have to acquire all the documents and we saw that you asked for and you received some documents. However, I'm interested whether you, during the time when you worked in the commission, had the documents of the forensics department that it made in August 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have them as a commission, but they were available.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
