utterances.text: As a commission, you made no inspection of the expertise of the found and seized weapons that was made in the forensics department of the ministry. In respect to that, I would like to ask you whether, in 2001, in the Ministry of Interior --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, the transcript did not record the answer of the witness -- of the witness to my previous question. The witness answered yes, but I can repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So I asked you whether you, as a commission, reviewed and had in mind the expertise that was produced on the found and seized weapons at that time.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, I'd like to ask you now, whether you, and bearing in mind that you worked in the uniformed police, and maybe you know this, did you have automatic rifles of Chinese production in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether -- could you repeat, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Whether the Ministry of the Interior, that is the police officers who were issued with those weapons, did you have rifles of Chinese made?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have, in 2001, automatic rifles Thompson of 45-millimetres calibre?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not within our armament.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have magazines for automatic rifles of Chinese make with 24 bullets?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had no armament of Chinese make.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have bullets of 45 millimetres calibre for the Thompson submachine-gun?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So if the analysis of weapons in your police forensics would state that such weapons did not exist within the Ministry of Interior, you also corroborate this, that such weapons did not exist there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, when working in the committee, did not have the documents that the department for internal affairs and the sector for internal affairs, Skopje, produced upon the request of the court and submitted to the prosecutor and the court. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My colleague asked you to -- asked me to ask you whether you had ammunition 7 times 62 of Chinese or Albanian make?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And maybe in order to have it completely clear, which weapons and which ammunition did you use?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The transcript reads only 62. This is 7.62. Could you tell us what weapons and what ammunition, I mean, what rifles you had at the time, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The automatic rifles were produced in what is now Serbia. Actually, the former Yugoslavia, the Zastava factory. Also, we had ammunition from the same factory, from Prvi Partizan Uzice and recently from the Samakov [phoen] factory in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, did you have or could you have had documents that the Prosecutor's office and the courts had available in 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you obtain or were you submitted some documents from the international organisations that were present at that time in Skopje, or in Republic of Macedonia, rather?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing was submitted to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In your method of work that you agreed, was it agreed that the commission members are not authorised to communicate the findings of the commission to other bodies and to the general public before the information, the final information, is submitted to the minister?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you explained answering to my colleague the Prosecutor, you invited quite a number of people to be interviewed. And as the documentation stands and also as it can be seen from the information that was produced, the first meeting of the committee took place on the 5th of May, 2003. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the information was produced on the 6th, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The commission member, Tanja Groseva, was not at that time meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Another person sat for her, another representative of the analytics department, although that person was not the committee member. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first meeting, according to that report, Gjorgji Mitrov, Zivko Gacovski, Johan Tarculovski, and Goce Ralevski were invited. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The first three persons, Gjorgji Mitrov, Zivko Gacovski and Johan Tarculovski were members of the MOI, while Goce Ralevski was not a MOI member?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zivko Gacovski was an employee of the Ministry of Interior as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, what I said was that only Goce Ralevski was not a MOI member?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Goce Ralevski was an employee of the parliament of the Republic of Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And out of all these persons invited, only Johan Tarculovski wrote an Official Note in his own hand. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, is it correct that on the 28th of May, the second meeting of the committee, you were not in attendance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And no other persons were interviewed during that meeting, only some documents were reviewed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is what the minutes read, that I was not in attendance, then I was not in attendance.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask that the witness is shown that document of the 28th. That is, I would like to ask that the witness please be shown on the screen Exhibit P435, marked for identification. You see this report now, General. In this information, in paragraph 3, it is stated that: "Responding to a telegramme from SVR Skopje a report was received, that over the aforementioned period of time in the area of Ljuboten village, the members of the active and the reserve forces of the SVR Skopje, police station Cair and the police station Mirkovci, were engaged at the check-points of Chinese wall, Straista, and Buzalak, check-points that were in operation before." It further states that: "On the 12th of August 2001, at about 1600 hours, in order to block the road between Ljuboten to Ljubotenski road and Cair the SVR Skopje established two platoons: One platoon of SVR Skopje and another from the Rapid Intervention Unit Lions. They had the task to provide conditions for safe transport of citizens who were leaving Ljuboten village and were on their way to Skopje, and they were gathered at the Buzalak location." General, General Risto Galevski gave evidence before this Court on the page 3766 to 3767 of the transcript. He stated the following: "[In English] When you learned in the afternoon that hundreds of villagers of Ljuboten were walking towards Skopje and that several thousand citizens from the neighbouring villages and Skopje were walking towards Radishani and that there had already been rather chaotic, that the citizens started turning cars over, that this was already known that there were injured among the villagers leaving the village, you then, as you testified, tried and in consultation with Bliznakovski, with Mitevski, and also in consultation with the minister, decided to sent to the site the posebna unit. Is that correct?" The answer was, Yes, it is correct. "[In English] As far as you know, one part of posebna was then deployed towards Radishani and Butel in order to create a tampon zone between the thousands of citizens and villagers from Ljuboten and in order to protect the police stations that these citizens do not enter the police station. Is that correct?" [Interpretation] The answer was, Exactly. "[In English] And you believe that through these efforts the police managed to prevent unforeseeable consequences that could have occurred on that day. Is that correct? Yes. Maybe we did not arrive in time to completely prevent contacts between the civilian population. They had already occurred to the extent that they did occurred but we prevented an incident of unforeseeable consequences that we did. [Interpretation] The question. [In English] So you already had an information that some of the villagers from Ljuboten were injured in the clash with a crowd and that some of these -- or one of these people was offered medical care in a hospital?" [Interpretation] The reply was: [In English] This is precisely why we have sent the posebna unit. [Interpretation] General, in his statement Goran Georgievski about whom you stated that in August 2001 he was the head of posebna units, in his statement dated the 5th of December, 2003, which he gave to the investigator Thomas Kuehnel, he stated the following in the paragraph 18: "[In English] On Sunday, 12th of August, between 15 and 16 hours, the under-secretary of police, General Risto Galevski called me and ordered me to send one platoon of the posebna police unit to the Cair police station. The order was to secure the Cair police station from the inside. Risto Galevski told me that certain events have taken place in Ljuboten and that different sorts of events could be expected from the population in Cair." [Interpretation] General, do you see a discrepancy between what is written in this telegramme sent by the SVR Skopje and this testimony?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me what is your knowledge, since you were the deputy to Mr. Galevski at the time, is it correct that the posebna unit was sent and that at that time as you testified yesterday, the Lions did not exist at all?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, the posebna unit from Skopje was the one to intervene, and it is also correct that the Lions had not been established yet.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the second page of this information, and that is N006-55025 in Macedonian, because the English version is still not -- oh, it is uploaded, but we haven't received it. But I will read it in Macedonian. "The commander of the anti-terrorist unit sent an information that over that period of time no members of that unit were employed. The then Rapid Intervention Unit Lavovi, the former Rapid Intervention Unit Lavovi because that unit had not been established then yet." Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this information, from the commander of the unit for anti-terrorist activities correspond to what you knew then at August 2001. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the anti-terrorist unit is actually Goran Georgievski who actually received the order from Risto Galevski to send the platoon of posebna. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The next meeting that you had was in November 2003, and you then interviewed Johan Tarculovski and Zoran Jovanovski, Bucuk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was the occasion when it was Johan Tarculovski only who was issued the caution that he can use an attorney and that he will be brought in if he does not respond to this invitation, and you never cautioned him about any other right then. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Tarculovski had left the Ministry of Interior then, and this is why he needed to be invited by a summons and he was issued then the caution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: But you did not inform him about the rights about which you need to inform a person against whom there is a criminal procedure or a disciplinary procedure initiated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is in the summons that he needs to come to be interviewed, and we did not caution him about other rights.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From the 12th until the 25th of November, as we can read in your information of 25th of November, apart from Johan Tarculovski you also interviewed Bucuk, Zoran Jovanovski, also Miodrag Stojanovski, Ljube Krstevski, Vanco Ginovski, Vladimir Cagorovic, Ljupco Bliznakovski, Pero Stojanovski, Trajce Kuzmanovski, and Radojko Lozanovski. These are the persons mentioned in your information dated 25th of November. Since it might be easier for us to work with the document, let's look at the number. That is 379, MFI but it is marked as 285. So Exhibit P379, MFI, while 65 ter number of the Prosecutor is 285.6. You see this information. Is that the last information that your commission produced?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, Johan Tarculovski was interviewed three times, actually twice, and the third time he wrote an Official Note in his own hand. Did you see that these three statements are completely different and absolutely contradictory to one another?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the first information dated 6th of May, if I reframe what it says, he stated that the minister Ljube Boskoski sent him to Ljuboten. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In his Official Note that he wrote on the same date when he was interviewed before the commission, he stated that the information that Xhavid Asani was in the village he heard from the villagers and he did not mention Ljube Boskoski at all. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the third statement, the one he gave on the 12th of November, 2003, he stated that he had made an arrangement with his buddies to go to the village. Do you remember that? This would be a rather free reframing of his ... Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I don't believe anywhere in the statement of Johan Tarculovski of the 12th of November that is part of this exhibit, Mr. Tarculovski refers to his buddies or friends. I believe a more accurate description would be that Mr. Tarculovski said he chose the persons who would accompany him to Ljuboten. He did not describe them in any more personal way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will then quote from the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: He stated that he came to Ljuboten upon his own motion because he wanted to come and he did not receive an order from anyone to go to Ljuboten village. And he stated that the persons who were at Ljuboten --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, and he stated that he decided not to disclose the names of those who were at Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, is this now what is written in your information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, you're a professional police officer. Did you trust any of these statements?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could any conclusion be drawn on the basis of these statements, and particularly any reliable conclusion on whether Johan was there and with whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is really a question for the Trial Chamber, not for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm requesting witness's opinion, whether he was able to draw a conclusion, and I know that this is the task for the Chamber once all evidence are presented, that the Chamber will decide about this fact, as well as on any other fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are not inclined to allow the question in that form which calls on the witness to be conjecturing about a matter which is for this Chamber in the end to determine. You may, if you wanted to, ask the witness whether in fact the commission reached conclusions about the presence of Mr. Tarculovski and with whom, but not go into this witness's opinion whether something was reliable or not. If that helps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, as a commission, and you as a president of the commission, on the basis of this information that were given to you by Johan Tarculovski were you able to determine whether Johan Tarculovski was in the village at all and with whom?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only from Johan's statements but also from the statements of other persons that were not employed in the ministry and were called for interview. As a commission we were not able to conclude what exactly took place there. Therefore, we wrote a final report to the minister that you have in your files and we told the minister that it would be the best to review decide on this case in an -- according to the professional manners, that is to say, by the bodies that are authorised to initiate certain procedures, criminal or misdemeanour procedures.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As a president of the commission, General, or as a commission were you able to conclude whether Ljube Boskoski had any connection with Johan Tarculovski in respect to the Ljuboten issue?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, since in these statements and I will freely interpret them now, the statement of Johan Tarculovski is included, that the minister authorised him to freely select the people and to arm -- and take arms. As a president of the commission and as a person who was a close associate to the minister, were you able to conclude whether the information that you received --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The form of that question combines the witness's role as a president of -- as the commission but also his status as a close associate to the minister, and so effectively is again asking the witness's personal opinion on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, were you able to reach any conclusion about the other facts regarding Minister Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: By "you," you mean the commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, commission. That was one of the tasks of the commission, Your Honours. I, therefore, ask about the commission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just making clear. Your question was were you able.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, okay. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're interested in the commission, not this individual.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the commission able to make a conclusion any fact regarding Ljube Boskoski about which Johan Tarculovski or other people spoke?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe it is a right time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have the second break and resume at five past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Residovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I put a document to the witness in tab 28.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the number, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Behind tab 98. I put to the witness a document number 65 ter 446 relating the village of Jezince, and after that I put to him part of the statement of Henry Bolton about the same area. So I would like the Chamber, since I failed to seek to tender it, I would seek to tender this document now as Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I haven't turned back to find it. I see there's no objection, so it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D187, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, based on the facts that you established, was the commission able to ascertain that some person has -- some person has committed a murder in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the documents and interviews that you had, was the commission able to ascertain what were the persons present in the village of Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the commission, based on the evidence and interviews that you had, able to ascertain whether a certain specific individual set on fire some house in Ljuboten?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the commission, based on the facts acquired, able to ascertain whether certain police officers mistreated some persons that were brought in, in the police stations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the commission, based on the facts acquired, able to ascertain whether some police officer at the check-points mistreated some person?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. General, you said that you had a decision of Minister Boskoski of the 13th of August, 2001 about the setting up of the first commission and you had the report of the first commission. My question is the following. Did only you had that report or was that report available to the other members of the commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you please explain what commission are you referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The decision in the report of the commission established by the Minister Boskoski. You said that you had -- that at the time when the second commission was operational that you had, I'm interested whether the other members of the commission also was -- were in the possession of that report or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have only read it and they didn't have it in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was Minister Hari Kostov who assigned the task to you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, did Minister Hari Kostov have that report created by the commission of Ljube Boskoski?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that on several occasions that you spoke with the minister about the work of your commission. I'm interested to know whether the minister gave you a task to review and examine the work of the first commission or he told you -- he told you not to do that part of the work or maybe he gave you some third task?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not have the task to review the work of the first commission, and he also did not indicate that we should analyse the work of the second commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement given to the OTP investigator, General Goran Mitevski stated that at the time of the work of your commission have met you and that he offered himself to come and be interviewed and he volunteered to give you other information. Do you remember meeting General Mitevski, and him offering you to -- to provide you with certain relevant information to give the relevant information to the commission?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we assessed that there is no need to do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You assessed that there is no need to interview him because of the fact that the minister told you that you should not pay attention to the work of the first commission, right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was that the reason that you did not call also other members of the commission to acquire certain facts of them or some evidence that they had available?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, if the police, already on 12th of August, in the afternoon hours, informed the investigating judge that they have information that there are killed persons in the village, in your opinion, would the police complete its task with it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after such an information, the further decision would be in the hands of the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he is the one who heads all the investigative actions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in that situation, the police would only be able to assist the judge and to carry out the tasks assigned to it by the judge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: General, in the second commission, did you bear in mind the report of the investigating judge, of the prosecutor, of the forensic pathologist from the Skopje sector, whereby it is clearly shown that these bodies made an effort to enter the village of Ljuboten on the 12th and the 14th?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know, General, that the investigating judge and the investigating team that he established was not able to enter the village?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, General, that without the on-site inspection it was not possible to examine the truthfulness of the information about the -- about the killed persons, about their number, about their capacity, about the way circumstances and causes of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, General, that the impossibility to determine those facts is -- was in fact an insufficient grounds for the police to file a criminal report against a known or unknown perpetrator?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, General, that -- that is also regulated with the rules for work of the bodies of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And if I may conclude, that means that the police -- in order for the police to file a criminal report, it had to acquire sufficient reliable evidence to establish a doubt that a person has committed an act that is a criminal act?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, suspicion, not doubt.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind that the prosecutor and the court have already been informed, you already said that the further competence and initiative was in the hands of the investigating judge and the prosecutor, was that the legal -- the lawful practice -- the legal practice in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a legal obligation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, General, that after the crime scene does not exist anymore because it has been changed with the burial of the killed persons, that the only way, in order to examine the mentioned relevant facts was to make an exhumation and to carry out a post-mortem of the buried killed persons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only way to -- to find out about the persons that have been buried was an exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind your professional experience, are you aware that the Law on Criminal Procedure of the Republic of Macedonia, an order or -- an exhumation can also -- may also be ordered by an investigating judge upon a proposal of the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, when in April 2002, when the post-mortem and the exhumation was carried out in the village of Ljuboten, you were at the position of the under-secretary in the Ministry of Interior. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the decision that appoints you to the second commission, the minister indicated that you should bear in mind the findings of the forensic medicine institute, that is to say, the post-mortem findings. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That was an important fact for any body that would examine the issue of the Ljuboten events. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you aware that after the report of the first commission, and based on suggestions derived from it, the exhumation and post-mortem was proposed by Minister Boskoski and that proposal was prepared also for the -- and was sent to the prosecutor and to the court by Goran Mitevski as director of the bureau for public security?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the document at tab 118. That is Exhibit 1D33, page -- okay, we can see it. Given that you had the information of the first commission, you know that the first commission finished its work and filed the information on 4th of September, 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: From this proposal, you can see that already on the 7th of September 2001, the Ministry of Interior, to the public prosecutor and the investigating judge on duty from the Skopje Court II filed a proposal for exhumation with a post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please now look in the document in tab 119.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: That is Exhibit P55. The page is N002-1146-003, and the English version is ET, N002-1148-N002-1148-1. General, you see this is an act of the public prosecutor's office dated 10th of September, 2001. Isn't it so?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the ministry promptly after the commission finished its work initiated a proposal on undertaking an exhumation and post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And that the prosecutor's office promptly after that proposal also reacted and proposed to the court to undertake certain investigating actions.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2 of this proposal, it is obvious -- it is visible that the public prosecutor's office in relation to this case acting pursuant to Article 148, paragraph 1, of the Code of Criminal Procedure and upon the written initiative of the Ministry of Interior, composed this proposal?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that in this way -- actually, the prosecutor's office has shown that the proposal of the ministry was accepted as an initiative because the ministry itself is not able to file a proposal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the work of the commission, were you in any way familiar that the investigating judge, immediately after receiving this proposal, took measures in order to carry out that investigating activity of exhumation and post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you gather that data in the performance of your duty or did you receive that data from the commission members or was it that you learned that information only afterwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We learned about them afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did the commission member, Besim Ramicevic, ever informed you - not you personally but the commission - that he was personally informed in the first steps of this initiative that was necessary to undertake other actions by the court?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not inform me, myself, and he did not inform the commission members.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document in tab 120. That is Exhibit 1D63, page, Macedonian, is N005-0754, and the English is N005-0754-ET. General, this is the Official Note that was submitted, as you can see here from the title, by Simeon Zidrovski and Besim Ramicevic. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Official Note was composed on the 18th of September, 2001, and it deals with the meeting of the 14th of September, 2001, at the premises of the forensics medicine and criminology institute. There was a consultation meeting initiated by the investigating judge of the Basic Court Skopje II, Mr. Dragan Nikolovski. In relation with actions undertaken according to the Article 244 of the Law on Criminal Procedure, the exhumation and the post-mortem of the persons killed in the village of Ljuboten in the course of the military operation that underwent in that region. Do you conclude from this that, on the basis of the initiative that came from the Ministry of Interior, the only possible legal procedure was undertaken, that of exhumation and post-mortem?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look now at the final paragraph of this Official Note on the first page, it reads here: "Dr. Aleksej Duma, expressed a preparedness to perform the exhumation and autopsy following a previously received order from the investigating judge indicating that, in order to avoid any subsequent distortion of the autopsy result of the buried remains in the village of Ljuboten, he will arrange for supervisors to be present during the investigation, namely, competent individuals from the Skopje office of the ICTY." Do you agree with me that from the very start, the persons who should have been involved in the exhumation and the post-mortem, were very transparent and wished to avoid any misunderstanding, so they immediately involved the representatives of the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with this.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you stated that you did not research the work of the first committee, you probably did not take into consideration all documents that that committee reviewed.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What does the yes mean? Did you take into consideration or did you not take?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not take documents into consideration. We did not look at them.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not know at all which actions were requested by the investigating judge for the police to perform and in what way and in what circumstances the police performed those tasks, regardless of whether it was department of internal affairs, Cair, sector for internal affairs, Skopje, or the ministry. You did not know that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Considering that the exhumation was performed during your term as an under-secretary, was it clear to you then that the international community was involved in the carrying out of the exhumation and the post-mortem and also were the representatives of the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could we please now look at the document in tab 126. That is Exhibit P55, and the page is N002-1146-029, and the English version is it at ET N002-1175-N002-1175-1. And while we're waiting for the document to be loaded, was it completely clear to you then that the exhumation in the village of Ljuboten could not have been performed without the assistance and the presence of the international community representatives?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that you see here, document produced by the basic public prosecutor's office on the 18th of March, 2002, that was sent to the Basic Court Skopje, to the investigative judge Dragan Nikolovski, and it is -- it deals with further specifying the exhumation order. The first paragraph reads: "Regarding the initiative of the MOI, the directorate for public security number 10-33282, dated 7th of September, 2001, to the title XXRO number 1098/01, dated 10th of September, 2001, in accordance with Article 148, paragraph 1 of the Law on Criminal Procedure a proposal was submitted regarding an undertaking certain investigation actions exhumation, from Article 244 of the Law on Criminal Procedure in order to examine and perform post-mortem of the bodies of unknown persons buried at the local cemetery in the village of Ljuboten to determine their identity, cause of death, time of death, the circumstances under which they met their death, since it was impossible to be done on the 13th and 14th of August, 2001, due to the well-known reasons the on-site inspection by the competent bodies was impossible." Do you see, General, that this request to indicate further details regarding the post-mortem order the basic public prosecutor's office indicates that the entire procedure was initiated from -- was based on the initiative of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can I say, could you agree with me on this, that when submitting this initiative, the minister and the ministry did more than the legal obligations were for them, and they started the procedure that was necessary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I think we are, again, asking this witness to draw a conclusion that is really for this Chamber at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I asked whether he could agree with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That doesn't help the problem. You're asking him whether the ministry and the minister complied with their legal obligations or did more than their legal obligations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is a legal issue, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You already stated that you did not have the task to research or investigate the work of the first committee.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you learn later that actually the minister immediately informed the coordination body of the government about all findings related to the Ljuboten events?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you, during the work of the committee or later, learn that the information that the first committee produced, after it was submitted to the minister, was forwarded to the government of the Republic of Macedonia and that the government of the Republic of Macedonia reviewed that information?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And is this the proper way for a minister to inform the government about a very important issue that is within the realm of his competences, to inform the government whose member the minister is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you at any later time, if you had not reviewed the documents produced by the first committee, did you learn that the minister informed the government later again, in November 2001?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When we spoke about the initiative for exhumation and post-mortem and for -- and about information that there are dead bodies buried in the village of Ljuboten, you stated that the police performed the task that it had under the law by doing this. Could you agree with me, General, if I say that after an information about an event that could be suspicious is received, the prosecutor is then the body or the person who decides on the further measures that need to be undertaken?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I will ask you now to look at the document in tab 101. That is Exhibit P46. The page is 0463-8774-044. I think we already have the document on the display. General, you see that this is the document by the Ministry of Interior, Cair department. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it was signed by the head of the department of internal affairs, Cair, Ljube Krstevski. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And it is sent to the basic public prosecutor's office, Skopje.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The correspondence stated that the prosecutor's office is sent analysis of fire-arm residue and the Official Note, number 537. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is written here as subject is also seen in the contents of this letter sent by Ljube Krstevski.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to turn to the document in tab 102. That is Exhibit P261, and the page is N005-1134, the English N005-1134-N005-1135-ET. It is again an act issued by the department for internal affairs, Cair, and at the remittal you see that this is the Official Note number 537. Is that correct? It is in tab 102.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this is precisely the Official Note that we saw mentioned in the previous document, that it was sent to the basic public prosecutor's office, Skopje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: This note contains information and findings about the death of Atulla Qaili.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me, General, that at the moment when the police informed the prosecutor's office about the death of a given individual that then, pursuant to the authorities vested in the prosecutor, the prosecutor was the person who needed to either carry out an investigation themselves or request the police to carry out the actions aiming at obtaining the additional information necessary for the prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now -- I would like to show you a part of the statement of the municipal prosecutor, Jovan Serafimovski, that is 65 ter 1D227, N002-2018. This is a statement that is available in the English language only. So 65 ter 1D227. This is the first page of the statement that the prosecutor, Jovan Serafimovski, made on the 19th and 20th of December to the investigator of the ICTY. Now I would like to show you the page 1D2454, paragraph 7. The Prosecutor states the follow: "[In English] In the request to conduct an investigation submitted on 14 August 2001, the name of Atulla Qani is mentioned. It was my obligation to ascertain the cause of death. I asked the investigative judge to inquire about this. We found out that Qani Atulla was injured during the clash with the police and army in Ljuboten. I was informed from the media that the police and army were there. I don't know which unit were there. I never receive information like this. I didn't ask for information like this." [Interpretation] Do you agree, General, with this, that it was actually the prosecutor, when he received this information, the one who had the duty to investigate it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When -- when the information about the death of a certain person reached the investigating judge, and not only about the death, about anything that would indicate that there is a suspicion a crime has been committed, then you agree me, then, this would be the duty for the investigating judge, to verify the facts and to inform the public prosecutor about it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask that 65 ter 1D547 be shown, page 1D5002, and in the English version is 1D4996. And that is the statement of the judge, Jovan Lazarevski, who made the statement on the 14th and the 19th of September, 2004, to the investigator and the Prosecutor of the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask now to move to page 2, 1D5003, and paragraph 4 in it, and the English page is 1D4998. The judge, Lazarevski, says the following: "As an investigating judge, pursuant to the law, I have the duty to safeguard the rights of the accused. For instance, the accused has the right to an attorney, the right to give a statement or refuse to give a statement, the right to call witnesses in his defence and the right to propose exculpatory evidence. The investigating judge is neutral, and if during the questioning of a defendant, information arises suggesting that the accused is innocent, the investigating judge must investigate those. As part of my office, I can ask for additional investigation or request additional evidence. Also, I can recommend that the investigation is terminated and the case be dropped if the evidence supports that decision. However, if I terminate the investigation and the public prosecutor disagrees with my decision, he or she can file an appeal against my decision." Do you agree, General, that this is the legal obligation and the right for the investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to look at the paragraph 9 at the page 1D5004 and the English page is 1D4999. And in this paragraph, the judge Lazarevski states the following: "It is quite possible that the investigation carried out into the events at Ljuboten was insufficient. In a normal situation, you should investigate both sides to a conflict. But in the case of Ljuboten, only the detained persons who were arrested at Ljuboten were investigated. The investigation suggested by the public prosecutor was carried out but no investigation was carried out into the actions of the Macedonian authorities at Ljuboten as it would have happened in normal circumstances. In my personal opinion, it is possible that this was an omission. Also witnesses were not heard because that was not suggested by the public prosecutor, so this was also probably an omission. In this case, due to certain security concerns, the investigating judge could -- was not able to carry out a full investigation. What happened in 2001 was madness which will pass." Do you agree with me, General, that what the judge Lazarevski says indicates that he had certain duties, obligations, and possibly omissions as well as omissions of the public prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Ministry of Interior could not influence the way in which the public prosecutor's office and the courts act. It could not have any type of influence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN JOVANOVSKI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient break, do you think, Ms. Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, maybe this would be the right time because I have another topic to move on to, so...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now, resume on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 17th day of September, 2007, at 2.15 p.m.
